problems.title: Lemma9.12 dual-vector construction does not generate the ambient module
problems.location: PDF50 Lemma9.12 proof; PDF51-53 basis changes; PDF53-55 dependency to9.14/9.15/10.1
assumptions: Even nonsingular form det-1 on free rank2 module
Free half-rank direct V, pluslagrangian, minuslagrangian complement
problems.proof:
## Core Lemma9.12: confirmed failed basis construction, complete replacement proof
Let Lambda=Z[T]/(T^2-1), P=Lambda x+Lambda v.
A=[[4(1-T),4-3T],[4-3T,6]], Q=[[2(1-T),4-3T],[0,3]].
A=Q+Q^t, det A=-1, even nonsingular. V=Lambda x is free half-rank direct.
A(+1)=[[0,1],[1,6]], so V+ is lagrangian.
A(-1)=[[8,7],[7,6]], and Z(v-x) is an isotropic direct complement to V-, hence lagrangian.
For the allowed basis completion x,v, the paper's uniquely prescribed u=A^{-1}x*=-6x+(4-3T)v.
lambda(x,u)=1, lambda(v,u)=0, but det[x,u]=4-3T is not a unit: evaluation at -1 is7.
Additive cokernel is Z/7 from [[4,-3],[-3,4]]. Thus the asserted generation on p50 fails with every lemma hypothesis.
Actual lagrangian complement is ell=v-(2+T)x: quadratic square0, cross lambda(x,ell)=T, determinant1. This is not a counterexample to Lemma9.12's conclusion.
Restriction Q|V=2(1-T) equals the actual genus1 Wall-form type (1-T)X1.
P50 wrong step is B(+1)L=I replaced by BL=I. P51 changes U+ and explicitly loses U+=E+(U1); p52 reuses that identity. Group as one core construction issue.
Dependency:9.12 ->9.14 ->9.15 ->10.1 and principal classification results. Major is based on damage to the essential argument, notwithstanding complete local repair.

Replacement:
Take any free complement U0 (Lemma3.9 supplies freeness). The chosen minus lagrangian is an integral graph relative V-+U0-. Lift its graph matrix via Z->Lambda, obtaining a free complement U with U-=L-.
In a basis V,U, write Gram[[A,Y],[Y^t,D]]. A(+)=0 and D(-)=0.
Nonsingular specializations imply detY(+),detY(-) are units in Z. Since Y(+) and Y(-) agree modulo2, their integral inverses do too. The fiber-product identity Lambda={(a+,a-): a+=a- mod2} lifts the inverse pair, so Y is invertible over Lambda.
Change U basis by Y^{-1}. Now cross block isI, A=(1-T)A0, D=(1+T)D0 with integral symmetric A0,D0. Ambient evenness implies every diagonal D0ii is even.
Choose integral C with C+C^t=-D0. Shift U by V(1+T)C. Its new Gram is D+(1+T)(C+C^t)+(1+T)^2 C^t A C=0.
The shifted module remains a half-rank direct complement. Cross block becomes I+A(1+T)C=I. Thus its annihilator equals itself, and it is lagrangian. This is a full proof of the repaired algebraic lemma.

problems.title: CorollaryD mod2 Euler contradiction incorrect
problems.impact: The invalid mod2 Euler inequality is the actual route to simple connectedness in the stated main involution application Corollary D. This is required for the Freedman identification of the orbit space with S4 and the application of Theorem A. The short local-monodromy replacement does not lower the severity of this core application proof failure. The diagonal antipodal quotient refutes only the auxiliary Euler inference, not all Corollary D branched-cover hypotheses.
problems.correction: Use the nontrivial local deck monodromy of a meridian to show it generates the exterior group Z2; the van Kampen quotient then kills this generator. Replace the Euler-characteristic inference, while retaining the correctly computed chi=2 and the final Freedman/Theorem A route.
problems.repair_verification: Exact calculation or analytic argument stated; no broader theorem refutation or independent external-library acceptance implied.

check.independent_reasoning: Root directly read source pp3-4: if the residual fundamental group were Z2, mod2 b1=b3=1, so chi=b2 rather than2+b2. The claimed contradiction is the printed route to simply connected orbit space, then S4 and Theorem A. The free diagonal-antipodal quotient demonstrates only the auxiliary Euler error. Under the actual branched-cover hypotheses, local meridian monodromy is nontrivial, generates the exterior Z2 and is killed in the van Kampen quotient; this is a new valid repair, not evidence that the original inference is harmless.
